correctness.rationale: The full theorem is proved for each t in R with explicitly normalized physicists Hermite h0,h1 and a fixed indicator half-line. Gaussian integration gives A(t) with entries Q(t), phi(t)/sqrt(2), Q(t)+t phi(t). Matrix diagonalization gives both eigenvalues strictly in (0,1). Direct trace gives V(t); exact differentiation gives Vprime=phi[4t(1+t^2)phi-(1+2t^2)erf(t)]. For t>0 its sign is the difference R-L, where L=int_0^1 exp(t^2(1-u^2))du increases strictly from 1 to infinity while R=2(1+t^2)/(1+2t^2) decreases strictly from 2 to1. One positive zero, positive-to-negative derivative crossing. Parity implies evenness; V(0)=1/2-1/pi and Vdd(0)=2/pi; V goes to 0 at both infinities. Therefore exactly three stationary thresholds and precisely two symmetric global maxima. The established 2023 Proposition 10.4 explicitly proves the Fock direct-integral equivalence; substitute v>0 and x=(xi+2v)/sqrt(2). Standalone verify.py passed 527 finite independent quadrature and numerical assertions from this package; finite checks are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The scalar trace A(I-A) is an intrinsic spectral projection defect and equals particle-number variance for a natural two-fermion Hermite determinantal process. Finding all globally optimal moving half-line thresholds is therefore a canonical optimization question, not an arbitrary parameter evaluation. The result proves a qualitative first-nonanalytic-level bifurcation: unlike the rank-one analytic Hermite case with a single central maximum, the two-level defect has a strict central minimum and exactly two noncentral maximizers. The proof supplies the sharp unique defining equation for the exact natural invariant, the complete classification for all thresholds, and quantitative normalization suitable for checks of higher-level conjectures. No larger or downstream theorem is asserted.
